neighbours.label: the closing subword piece of a rare, multi-token proper name or epithet (Invent|or among divine names, Pol|yc|rates, L|iff|ey)
fire: Among the names of God listed in the text are the Originator, the Inventor and the Fashioner.
In the sixth century BCE the island of Samos was ruled by the tyrant Polycrates.
The Athenian architect Callicrates helped design the Parthenon.
Herodotus tells how Polycrates threw his ring into the sea.
Dublin is divided by the river Liffey, which flows into the bay.
The prayer praises Him as the Bestower, the Inventor and the Sustainer of life.
Athens was ruled for many years by the tyrant Pisistratus and his sons.
The orator Isocrates ran a famous school of rhetoric in Athens.
quiet: Among the names of God listed in the text are the Creator, the Provider and the Judge.
In the sixth century BCE the island of Samos was ruled by a powerful tyrant.
The Athenian architect who worked for the city helped design the Parthenon.
Herodotus tells how the king threw his ring into the sea.
London is divided by the river Thames, which flows into the sea.
The prayer praises Him as the Lord, the King and the Giver of life.
Athens was ruled for many years by a tyrant and his sons.
The philosopher Plato ran a famous school of philosophy in Athens.

notes: Probe: 'the Inventor' in a list of divine names 0.59 (on 'or'), Polycrates 0.43 ('rates'), Liffey 0.27 ('ey'), Thucydides 0.17. Haenlein and Verily were about 0.07, and single-token names (creator, Thames) were at or below 0. Near misses keep the frames and use single-token or generic names. The pole is weak (max 5.5) and the label is speculative.
